Rashi on Nedarim 28a:10:1.english: One may not initiate to him with an oath - That he should not say to him, "If you wish, I will swear to you."

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:10:2.hebrew: הא בנדר יפתח לו - שיאמר לו: אם תרצה, אדור לך נדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:10:2.english: But with a vow he may initiate to him - [Meaning] that he may say to him: "If you wish, I will vow a vow to you."

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:11:1.hebrew: הא מינדר נדר ליה בשבועה - אם הליסטים מזקיקו לכך, וידור לו כן בלשון שבועה כדאמרן לעיל:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:11:1.english: But he may vow to him with an oath - If the bandit compels him to do so, he may vow to him thus in the language of an oath, as we said above.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:11:2.english: But didn't we learn, etc. - And why does it teach in the baraita that he may not initiate with an oath to him?

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:12:1.hebrew: תריץ הכי תנא במתני' בנדר להודיעך כחן דבית שמאי - דאפילו בנדר גרידא לא, וכ"ש בנדר שבועה:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:12:1.english: [The Gemara] answers thus: It taught in the Mishna concerning a vow to convey to you the force of Beit Shammai['s opinion] - For even with a mere vow [it is] not [permitted], and all the more so with a vow [of] an oath.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:12:2.hebrew: וברייתא תנא בשבועה להודיעך כחן דב"ה - דאפי' בשבועה יפתח לו. וברייתא משום ב"ה נשנית, ולאו דוקא היא, ולא מצית למימר התם בשבועה הוא דלא יפתח וכו', ולא מקשינן דב"ש אדב"ש:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:12:2.english: And the baraita taught [the halakha] regarding an oath to convey to you the strength of [the opinion of] Beit Hillel - That even with an oath he may initiate [it] for him. And the baraita was taught on account of Beit Hillel, and it is not [to be taken] strictly; thus you cannot say there [that] it is [only] with an oath that he may not initiate, etc., and we do not raise a contradiction between [the ruling of] Beit Shammai [there] and [that of] Beit Shammai [here].

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:13:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר הכי קתני - האי לא יפתח דברייתא, לא משמע כדאמרינן דבאונסין קאי, אלא האי לא יפתח — דב"ש סברי לא יפתח לו החכם פתח לחרטה להשאל על שבועתו, דאין שאלה לשבועה לפני החכם. וליכא למידק מינה שום קושיא:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:13:1.english: Rav Ashi said: This is what it is teaching - This [statement,] "he may not open," in the baraita does not mean as we said [earlier], that it refers to [vows taken under] coercion; rather, this "he may not open" [means] that Beit Shammai hold that the Sage may not open for him an opening for regret to request [dissolution] of his oath, since there is no request [for dissolution] of an oath before the Sage. And there is no difficulty at all to be inferred from it.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:14:1.english: [If] he said, "These saplings are an offering" - That is to say, that they should be consecrated.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:14:2.hebrew: אם אינן נקצצות - היום, מוקי לה בגמרא; ועבר היום ולא נקצצו ולא נשרף הטלית, הרי הן הקדש ויש להן פדיון, והדמים יכנסו להקדש והם יצאו לחולין:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:14:2.english: If they are not cut [down] - [Meaning] today, [as] it is established in the Gemara; and [if] the day passed and they were not cut [down] or the garment was not burned, behold, they are consecrated and are subject to redemption, and the money enters [the] Temple [treasury] and they go out to non-sacred [status].

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:14:3.hebrew: אבל אם אמר הרי הנטיעות האלו קרבן עדי שיקצצו אין להם פדיון - לעולם, כל זמן שלא נקצצו, ואין יוצאין לחולין, אלא קדושות הן, שהן בקדושת הגוף לעולם, ואין להם תקנה עולמית, שאפילו פדאן — חוזרות וקדושות. דכיון דאמר עד שיקצצו, אין להם פדיון לעולם כל זמן שלא נקצצו; משמע דלעולם יהיו קרבן עד שיקצצו:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:14:3.english: But if he said, "These saplings are an offering until they are cut down," they have no redemption - [They have no redemption] ever, as long as they have not been cut down, and they do not go out to non-sacred status; rather, they remain consecrated, for they have inherent sanctity forever, and they have no remedy ever, for even if he redeemed them, they revert to being consecrated. For since he said, "until they are cut down," they have no redemption ever as long as they have not been cut down; [this phrasing] implies that they shall forever be an offering until they are cut down.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:1:1.english: Except for by an oath - That he should not say, "May [all] the fruits in the world be forbidden to me by an oath if they are not terumah."

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:2:1.hebrew: לא יפתח לו בנדר - אם הליסטים אינו מזקיקו שידור, לא יפתח לו הוא בעצמו:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:2:1.english: One should not initiate by [taking] a vow for him - If the robber does not compel him to take a vow, he himself should not initiate [it] for him.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:2:2.hebrew: במה שהוא מדירו - בלבד ידור ולא בדבר אחר, כדמפרש:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:2:2.english: About that which he compels him to vow - Only [that] may he vow, and not about another matter, as [it] explains.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:3:1.english: How [so]? He said to him, etc., his wife is permitted to him - For that is what he is making him vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:3:2.english: And his children are prohibited - For that is regarding what he did not compel him to vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:4:1.hebrew: דינא דמלכותא דינא - ולאו נדרי אונסין נינהו, ואמאי נודרין למוכסין להבריח המכס של מלכות:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:4:1.english: The law of the kingdom is the law - And [thus] they are not vows [made under] duress, so why may one vow to tax collectors to evade the tax of the kingdom?

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:5:1.english: Who has no fixed amount - For he takes whatever he wants.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:5:2.english: To a tax collector who establishes himself on his own - That it is not of the kingdom.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:7:1.hebrew: כיון דאמר יאסרו - ולא אמר מילתא דהערמה, איתסרו ליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:7:1.english: Since he said, "They shall be forbidden" - and he did not say a matter of evasion, they become forbidden to him.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:7:2.hebrew: אי דאמר היום לא מקבל מיניה מוכס - ואינו מניחו בשביל אותו נדר שלא יטול הפירות, שהרי שומע דבהערמה נדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:7:2.english: If he says: Today, the tax collector will not accept [it] from him - And he does not leave him [alone] on account of that vow [such] that he would not take the produce, for he hears that he vowed with artifice.

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:8:1.english: Where he says in his heart, "Today":

Rashi on Nedarim 28a:8:2.english: [They] are not [significant] matters - In general.

Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:13:1.hebrew: וב"ה אומרים יש שאלה בשבועה - פי': נזקקין להתיר לו. ולמ"ד לעיל (נדרים דף כב:) "אין נזקקין לאלהי ישראל", מוקי הך דב"ה דהכא בנדר בודאי, אי נמי בשבועה, רק [לא] הזכיר שם שמים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:13:1.english: And Beit Hillel say there is a request [for dissolution] of an oath - Explanation: [The sages] attend [to his request] to permit [the oath] for him. And according to the one who said earlier (Nedarim 22b), "We do not attend [to an oath taken] by the God of Israel," he certainly establishes this [statement] of Beit Hillel here as [referring to] a vow, or else to an oath [where] he merely did [not] mention the Divine Name.

Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:14:1.hebrew: הרי נטיעות האלו קרבן - הכא מיירי שמתפיס להו לדמי קרבן ממש, דלא מיירי בקונמות, מדלא אמר "כקרבן". ואפילו לר"מ, דלא שנא בין "הקרבן" ל"קרבן", דבכל ענין יחול אסור קונם — ה"מ כשאוסר האיסור או עליו או על חבירו, כגון שאמר "ככר זו קרבן או עלי או עליך"; אבל כאן, שאמר "קרבן" סתמא, ואינו מדכיר קרבן גבי שום אדם, הלכך ע"כ לדמי קרבן אמר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:14:1.english: These saplings are an offering - Here [the Mishnah] is speaking of [a case] where he consecrates them for the value of an actual offering, for it is not speaking of konam vows, since he did not say "kekorban" [like an offering]. And even according to Rabbi Meir, for whom there is no difference between "hakorban" [the offering] and "korban" [an offering], such that in either case the prohibition of a konam takes effect — that applies [only] when he forbids the item either upon himself or upon his fellow, such as when he said, "This loaf is an offering, whether upon me or upon you"; but here, where he said "an offering" unspecified and does not mention "an offering" with respect to any person, therefore he necessarily meant [it] for the value of an offering:

Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:14:2.hebrew: אם אינן נקצצות - כגון דאיכא זיקא נפישא כדאמר בגמ', וסבור הוא שלא יוכלו לימלט מן הרוח. וכן "טלית זו אם אינה נשרפת" — כגון דאיכא דליקה, וסבור שלא יוכל לימלט מן האש. ואפילו הכי "יש להן פדיון", כלומר: הם קדושים, ופדיון מועיל בהם; ואגב דקתני בסיפא "אין להן פדיון", תנא נמי ברישא "יש להם פדיון", אבל עיקר חידוש — ממה שהם קדושים, כדפירשתי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:14:2.english: If they are not cut down - For example, when there is a strong wind, as it says in the Gemara, and he thinks that they will not be able to escape the wind. And similarly, "This garment [is an offering] if it is not burned" — for example, when there is a fire, and he thinks that it will not be able to escape the fire. Even so, "they are subject to redemption" — that is to say, they are consecrated, and redemption is effective for them; and incidentally, because [the Mishnah] teaches in the latter clause "they are not subject to redemption," it also teaches in the former clause "they are subject to redemption," but the main novelty is that they are consecrated, as I have explained:

Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:4:1.hebrew: והא אמר שמואל דינא דמלכותא דינא - פי' בב"ק (דף קיג):
Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:4:1.english: "But didn't Shmuel say: The law of the kingdom is the law?" - [This is] explained in Bava Kamma (113).

Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:5:1.hebrew: במוכס שאין לו קצבה - ואין תאמר: מכל מקום דינא דמלכותא הוא? וי"ל: כיון שאין דרך המוכסין כך, אין זה דינא אלא גזילה של מוכס עצמו. ואע"ג דסבירא לן דברים שבלב אין דברים, לגבי אונסין שרו רבנן. וא"ת: הא לעיל (נדרים דף כ:) גבי ד' נדרים התירו בלא שום אונס, אף על גב דהוה דברים שבלב הוויין דברים! וי"ל, דהתם היינו טעמא משום דאנן סהדי שדעתו לכך, וכיון דאנן סהדי — הרי כאילו פירש בהדיא, ולא הוי דברים שבלב; אבל הכא ליכא למימר אנן סהדי אי לאו האונס, ובין תלמיד חכם ובין עם הארץ מיתסר בלא אונס כשאמר בלבו "היום", כיון דלא שייך אנן סהדי. וההיא דרבי עקיבא שנשבע ומבטלה בלבו (במסכת כלה) — התם נמי הוי אונס, שהיה צורך גדול לידע לברר על אותו עז פנים שהיה ממזר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28a:5:1.english: To a tax collector who has no fixed amount - And if you will say: Nevertheless, it is the law of the kingdom [dina demalkhuta]? One can answer: Since this is not the [standard] practice of tax collectors, this is not [valid] law, but rather robbery by the tax collector himself. And even though we hold [that] unspoken thoughts in the heart are not [legally] significant words, regarding cases of duress, the Rabbis permitted [it]. And if you will say: Behold, earlier (Nedarim 20b), regarding [the] four vows, they permitted [them] without any duress — even though they were unspoken thoughts in the heart, they were [considered legally] significant words! One can answer that there, that is the reason: because we are witnesses [anan sahadei, i.e., it is self-evident] that his intention was for that, and since we are witnesses — behold, it is as if he stated [it] explicitly, and it is not [merely] unspoken thoughts in the heart; but here, one cannot say "we are witnesses" were it not for the duress, and both a Torah scholar and an unlearned person [am ha'aretz] are prohibited [by the vow] without duress when he said in his heart "today," since "we are witnesses" does not apply. And [as for] that [incident] of Rabbi Akiva, who swore and nullified it in his heart (in Tractate Kallah) — there too it was a case of duress, for there was a great need to know [and] to clarify concerning that brazen person that he was a mamzer.
